design: Abstract lab domain, candidate ID and fact-key schema; candidate pool visible at snapshot clock 0
Immutable full roster stored with frozen catalogs, never minted from incoming visible records by replay
Policy sees no outcome/utility labels; Stop Oracle sees no Decision
Verifier imports contracts and read-only fixture loader only; independently recomputes execution and metrics
B0/B1 share eligibility and visible safety information; B1 only ablates scoring feedback
integration_requirements: Genuine candidate snapshot and domain authority boundary

rules.must_stop: domain UNKNOWN, time/step cap, empty pool, or no eligible candidate
rules.opportunity: fresh eligible candidate in frozen worthwhile_ids
rules.uncertainty: conflict, no trustworthy records, or no prescribed fresh utility

tested: 24 development plus 12 exposed holdout cases, 108 policy runs
78 real CLI negative executions including 12 compound variants
candidate/evidence iteration permutation yields byte-identical replay
Git readback of 18 source/reference blobs and GitHub contracts API readback
tradeoffs: Fewer generic facts and bounded pools make exhaustive local inspection cheap
Shared schema/provenance concepts may still cause common-mode errors despite separate arithmetic
Fresh worthwhile labels are a chosen normative objective, not empirical optimal stopping
Exogenous feedback enables fair visibility but cannot establish action-caused information gain
